table.ruleB: WIP limits, upper marks, lower marks, start counts, target 38 and tally 0 are the same numbers; all teams start ROUTINE; New Tickets table is the same

table.ruleA: Add row k, column i of the input to x_i; no bound enforced
table.ruleB: Add the team's new tickets for the sprint; WIP limit not enforced

table.ruleA: Sequential (Gauss-Seidel) order 1..6, each using the value already updated; if x_i > c_i (strictly) then v = x_i - c_i, x_i = c_i, v goes to i+1, and for component 6 to s
table.ruleB: Sequential order 1..6, excess from team n reaches team n+1 before it is handled; if count > WIP limit (strictly) the excess goes downstream and the count is set to the limit; team 6's excess goes to the closed tally

table.ruleA: Read after Step 2. INACTIVE and x_i >= u_i becomes ACTIVE; ACTIVE and x_i <= d_i becomes INACTIVE; otherwise no change; at most one change; record (iter, comp, before, after)
table.ruleB: Read after step 2. ROUTINE and count >= upper becomes ESCALATED; ESCALATED and count <= lower becomes ROUTINE; otherwise no change; at most one change; recorded the same way

table.ruleA: Simultaneous (Jacobi): amounts come from the start-of-step values and the Step-3 flags. INACTIVE gives floor(x/4) to s; ACTIVE gives floor(x/2) to i-1, and component 1 gives it to s; every x_i falls by its own t_i; no bound
table.ruleB: All amounts are worked out first from the start-of-step counts. ROUTINE closes floor(n/4) to the tally; ESCALATED bounces floor(n/2) to the previous team, and team 1 sends it to the tally; bounced-in tickets do not change amounts already worked out; no limit

table.ruleA: If the 1-norm is strictly > 38, every one of the six components becomes floor(x_i/2) and the removed x_i - floor(x_i/2) (the ceiling half) goes to s; the iteration is recorded; 38 or less does nothing
table.ruleB: If the total is strictly > 38, every team closes ceil(n/2) to the tally and keeps the rest (= floor(n/2)); the sprint is recorded; 38 or less does nothing

table.ruleA: After Step 5 of iteration 5: (a) end values 1-6, (b) flags, (c) flag changes, (d) penalty iterations, (e) s, (f) balance check
table.ruleB: After step 5 of sprint 5: (a) end counts 1-6, (b) statuses, (c) status changes in order, (d) halving sprints or 'never', (e) closed tally, (f) balance check with both sides written out
table.difference: Presentation only: B asks for both sides of the balance check to be written out and for 'never fired' to be stated. The reported values are the same.

result.probeWhy: The probe starts high and sends all 9s in cycle 1, which forces a full overflow cascade from position 1 to 6 with spill into the loss tally. That tests sequential against simultaneous overflow and the strict '>' bound. Every position then trips the upper threshold at once, so position 1 sends its transfer to the tally. The zero row in cycle 2 lets values fall to the lower thresholds, which tests '<=' de-escalation. Alternating 9/0 rows and odd totals make the line-wide halving fire repeatedly on odd counts, which tests floor-kept against ceiling-removed. The arithmetic was done with a script (sim.py in the P08 folder) that codes each document separately as written. The script also ran 200,000 random starting and input tables (0 to 9) with 0 mismatches, which covers the equality-at-38 and threshold-equality cases the hand-built probe may not hit.
